nodes.question: Comparing the source and edited images, is the front overlap of the woman’s bright pink jacket reliably visible enough to determine whether it became more closed? Assess actual jacket-panel overlap or closure, not changes caused only by pose, motion, or viewpoint.
nodes.criteria: complete: the front is visibly fully closed in the edited image. partial: reliable comparison shows increased front-panel overlap or other visible closing progress, but the jacket is not fully closed. absent: reliable comparison shows no visible closing progress, or the front is visibly less closed; an open jacket alone is not sufficient if pose or viewpoint prevents comparison. unknown: the front overlap or change cannot be reliably judged because it is occluded, turned away, or obscured by pose, motion, or viewpoint.
nodes.binding: Visual target: the woman’s bright pink outer jacket. Compare the front panels and their overlap in source and edited images. Distinguish actual closure or increased overlap from the jacket swinging outward or apparent changes due to pose or viewpoint; use unknown if comparison is unreliable.

program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.
